items.title: Carlos Alcaraz beats Ben Shelton in final-set tie-break to reach ATP Finals final – as it happened
items.summary: Alcaraz started slowly but finished emphatically to defeat the US Open runner-up 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (1) and advance to the season-ending final for the second straight yearSo who wins today? Well, so much depends on Alcaraz’s physical condition. If his hamstring doesn’t hinder him, he should win, given the heights he’s hit this week and during the past two months. His shot-making was devastating against Cobolli yesterday, when he deliberately kept the points short and sharp to protect his injury. First-strike tennis is Shelton’s forte, though, so expect plenty of indoor fireworks between these two showmen and explosive hitters. And being a left-hander, Shelton will hope his ferocious cross-court forehand can stretch Alcaraz on the backhand side and put pressure on that injured hamstring. Shelton’s biggest weapon, of course though, is his serve.As for the head-to-head, Alcaraz leads 4-1, with Shelton’s only victory coming in that US Open quarter-final in September. Alcaraz has beaten Shelton indoors twice before: in the Paris Masters final two weeks ago and at the Laver Cup in 2024. Continue reading...

items.title: SNL’s skit Sister captures the quiet agony of caregiving for women: ‘I’ve never felt seen like that’
items.summary: The viral satirization of the caregiving burden left to women and daughters hit home for many viewersThe Saturday Night Live sketch, titled Sister quickly went viral this week for its satirization of the burden that women and daughters face to take care of aging family members. In the parody commercial, comedian John Mulaney touts the benefit of “Sister”, who he describes as “a live-in 24/7 elder care provider that is completely free, and also your sister” . “Now I don’t have to worry about dad getting the care and attention he needs because my sister will do it, and I can get back to my life, and the stuff I like to do,” Mulaney says, as the sister, played by cast member Jane Wickline, gives their father’s medication to him.The sketch, which amassed over seven million views on YouTube in less than a week since it aired, has received thousands of responses and comments about its accuracy. “This is one of the MOST wicked and spot on SNL sketches ever written,” wrote one commenter on YouTube. Another posted: “As a hospice nurse this definitely tracks. I deal 90% of the time with adult daughters, and if there is no daughter, it is the daughter in law.” “This is so real it almost gave me a stroke from rage,” added another viewer. Continue reading...

items.title: Noah Okafor piles on pain for Alonso as rampant Leeds demolish dismal Chelsea
items.summary: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since returning to the top of the table with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty early in a one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that it was easy to conclude they would have won even without a helping hand from the officials. items.title: Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start
items.summary: New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted that the new manager bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row.Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard said. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.” Continue reading...

Tottenham have struggled to match their London rivals Arsenal and Chelsea’s record of producing homegrown players in recent years but they appear to have struck gold with Williams-Barnett. This, Amazon says, is the “symphony of people and technology” to which the retail giant owes its success.Following a barrage of negative publicity about working practices, Amazon began to open up its fulfilment centres to carefully controlled free public tours a decade ago. items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI appears to mock NFL sexual misconduct scandals in radio parody
items.summary: Comedian Stavros Halkias voices fictional shock jockSegment echoes Watson, Tucker misconduct allegationsRockstar’s latest skewers American sports cultureThe long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI appears to have taken aim at the NFL’s sexual misconduct scandals – and the culture of excuses surrounding them – with a satirical segment on the video game’s fictional conservative talk radio station bearing striking similarities to allegations against Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson and Kansas City Chiefs kicker Justin Tucker.The segment features comedian and voice actor Stavros Halkias defending Anthony Ross, a fictional player for the Vice City Manatees, after an “alleged” incident involving a team masseuse. Although neither Watson nor Tucker are mentioned by name, the circumstances closely resemble allegations made against both players. Continue reading...

items.title: Washington Spirit provide hope and joy in a city that badly needs it
items.summary: Spirit’s run to the NWSL Championship final is in part based on a positive connection with fans at a time when DC is troubled in more ways than oneIn the moments after the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals last weekend, all of Audi Field was in rapture. In the stands, around 20,000 Spirit supporters had filled the stadium to capacity, the sixth time they’d done so in 2026. They filled the place with the type of wondrous noise that’s become alien in DC sports in recent years, the type of gleeful adoration reserved for the city’s rare winners. The Spirit will return to their home stadium to face the Kansas City Current in the NWSL championship this Saturday.In short order, the Spirit’s players made their way to the north end of the stadium, taking their celebrations into the crowd with their supporters. Perhaps no player has done more to push the Spirit into not only local but national relevance than US women’s national team forward Trinity Rodman, and Rodman herself grabbed a flag from a fan, jubilantly waving it above the crowd. Moments later, she bolted back onto the field and track down the club’s owner, Michele Kang, cajoling the businesswoman into a celebratory dance. Continue reading...

items.title: The Super Bowl of F1: how Las Vegas GP has hit the jackpot after turbulent start
items.summary: George Russell calls it the biggest race on the Formula One calendar bar Monaco – and the numbers back him upThat Formula One has achieved a palpable success in hosting a race in Las Vegas is impossible to ignore. Even with this year’s outing a dead rubber and with the city in perhaps its least flattering light, the cold drizzle of a Thursday afternoon beneath gunmetal-grey skies, the fans who have flocked to Nevada were irrepressibly enthusiastic.Long queues stretched out into the streets before the gates were even open and it seems many locals who were initially cool to the somewhat disruptive F1 circus have embraced the fans, their fervour for the sport and the positive impact of the race.
